clue.text: An identity thief, Neo's following the monarch

parts.note: Neo is the setter, so 'Neo's' stands for 'I am', shortened to I'M
POST- is the prefix meaning after or following
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard monarch

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a fraudster who has stolen someone's identity and is now trailing the king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym is the giveaway: 'Neo's' reads as 'Neo is', i.e. I'M from the setter's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who pretends to be another person, as an identity thief does, is a fraud passing under a false name.

clue.text: Scrooge is in sea abroad

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the foreign word for sea

parts.note: MER is French for sea, the foreign word signalled by 'abroad'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dickens's famous skinflint has gone off sailing overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to take the sea in French, MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge from A Christmas Carol is the archetypal hoarder of money, so his name is a byword for a skinflint.

clue.text: Why his beef is not with me?

definitions.text: Why his beef is not with me?

parts.words: Why his beef is not with me?
parts.note: beef read as a meal rather than a grievance: what one person enjoys eating another finds harmful, as the proverb says of tastes

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled that another person's quarrel is not directed at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a complaint, but it is meat: the dish he relishes would not agree with me, which is the proverb about differing tastes.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says tastes differ: something one person loves can be harmful or hateful to someone else.

clue.text: Test cases sorted out in class

indicators.note: the word for a test encases, or holds, the other letters

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: sorted means put in order afresh, so the word out is rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Exam scripts graded during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test cases' reads as examples for testing, but 'cases' is a verb meaning encloses, and 'sorted' rearranges the word 'out' to fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session, a kind of class held with a tutor.

clue.text: Body-snatchers, not unknown in cemetery, beaten with iron urns

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
not tells you to leave the unknown letter out of the burial ground word

parts.note: taken as written
Y, like X and Z, is a mathematical unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grave robbers who dropped something unknown in a graveyard and were attacked with metal vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: CEMETERY without Y gives CEMETER; with IRON URNS those fifteen letters are 'beaten' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteenth-century grave robbers who dug up corpses to sell to anatomists were known by this name.

clue.text: See 3
Rodent in baked dish for buccaneer

indicators.note: the rodent goes inside the pastry dish

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent baked into a pie, served to a sea rover.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer is a sea robber, specifically one of the Caribbean freebooters, so a straight synonym.

clue.text: One ahead something charged?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
on means forward or ahead, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: Someone moving into the lead, wondering what they are being billed for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a fee, but it means carrying an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule carrying electrical charge is so called in chemistry and physics.

clue.text: Mature mother holding son in work of art

parts.note: old means mature, grown on in years

indicators.note: the word for mother holds the son's letter inside

parts.note: MATER is Latin for mother, used in English public-school slang

explanation.surface: An older mother cradling her son in a painting, like a Madonna and Child.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a great European painter before about 1800 and a painting by one, so a work of art.

clue.text: Start on alpine trail for this!

definitions.text: Start on alpine trail for this!

indicators.note: the start of the word alpine, its opening letter

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds

explanation.surface: Begin on a mountain path if you want to do this!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: setting off on a mountain trail is how you begin a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb up a mountain is what an alpine trail leads to, the act of going upwards.

clue.text: Still holding an old penny piece

indicators.note: the calm word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: serene means still, calm
A, the indefinite article
D stood for the old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Someone still hanging on to an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the abbreviation for a penny in Britain's pre-decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece sung or played to a loved one, usually under a window at night.

clue.text: Roman Catholic in boat's Middle Ocean killer

indicators.note: the church abbreviation sits inside the other letters
the middle of the word boat, its two central letters

explanation.surface: A Catholic sitting in the middle of a boat, menaced by a killer of the seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' takes the two central letters of the vessel's name, and 'in' sets the church abbreviation between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is the sea's top predator, so a fair description of the creature.

clue.text: Someone from Zenda or Turin an IRA suspect?

indicators.note: suspect suggests something dodgy or not right, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a person from Zenda, Turin or the IRA under suspicion?
explanation.walkthrough: Zenda is the fictional kingdom's town in Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Zenda is set in Ruritania, the imaginary Central European kingdom of Hope's novel, so a native comes from there.

clue.text: Town knight and soldiers that catch MP by leg

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the word that catches, or encloses, the MP's letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ON is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A knight and troops in some town grab a Member of Parliament by the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Northampton is a county town in the English Midlands, known for shoemaking.

clue.text: Songs at speed in controlled atmosphere?

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
pace means speed

explanation.surface: Music played fast in a room with regulated climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled atmosphere' suggests air conditioning, but it is the sky over a country under air-traffic control.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's sky region is regulated by air-traffic controllers, a playful reading of an atmosphere under control.

clue.text: See 3
Books in scripture studies for mechanical routine

indicators.note: the books go inside the school subject

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, the school subject
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Biblical books taught in religious classes by mindless repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means mechanical repetition without understanding, so a routine done by habit.

clue.text: If I stop uprising, sergeant major finds non-violent way

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cap is to put a stop or limit on something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior soldier decides that halting a rebellion should be done peacefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a rebellion; it reverses CAP to PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that disputes should be settled without war or force, a way of life rejecting violence.

clue.text: Democrat welcome for Cameron

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A Democrat greets the former British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was UK Prime Minister 2010 to 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The short first name of David Cameron, former British Prime Minister, so an example of who Cameron is.

clue.text: School workers crying about Guevara

indicators.note: the crying word goes around the revolutionary's name

parts.note: tears are what crying produces
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: Staff at a school weeping over the revolutionary Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Those employed in schools to instruct pupils, a straightforward description.

clue.text: Girl first victim under Islamic State

indicators.note: in a down clue, the victim comes beneath the other abbreviation

parts.note: Abel, killed by Cain, was the first murder victim in Genesis

explanation.surface: A girl becomes an early casualty under the rule of a terrorist group.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female forename, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Perhaps most senior educationalist

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be in another order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: The most senior person in education, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian educator whose child-centred teaching method bears her name.

clue.text: See 3
Name deadly female hidden in old province

indicators.note: the female letter is hidden away, taken out of the deadly word

parts.note: fatal means deadly

explanation.surface: A deadly woman concealing herself in a former province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it removes F.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994, when it became KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: Winged beings caught by current in swirling Humber

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the current's letter sits inside the rearranged river name
swirling water churns things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Angels caught in the eddying waters of the Humber estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges HUMBER to HERUBM, and 'in' puts I between its B and M. The Humber is an English estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are angels of the second order, depicted with wings, so winged heavenly creatures.

clue.text: Gentleman, hungry, eats sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer is held inside the words

explanation.surface: A gentleman who is hungry tucks into some sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food; it signals a hidden word. RYE is Romany for gentleman, as in George Borrow's The Romany Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: In Romany, rye means a gentleman, a sense kept alive in English by Borrow's book title.

clue.text: Completely hot dog Dorothy had

parts.note: in means fashionable, the hot thing
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Dorothy's dog was thoroughly overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, entirely, so a synonym for totally.

clue.text: Gold pleasing Blair

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
well means satisfactory or pleasing, as in 'all is well'

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is pleased with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair, but it is Eric Blair, the real name of George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair, author of Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Lion Man's reinvented harmonics

indicators.note: reinvented means made over in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A lion-man figure's musical overtones given a new form.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lion Man is a prehistoric ivory figurine.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell tuning the nominal is one of the main overtones or partials, so these are a bell's harmonics.
